summary: This subsystem handles authentication, theming, top-level provider composition, and the entire navigation tree for the Carben Connect Mobile 2.0 app. App.js composes nested context providers (Theme, Auth, Notification, QuickBooks) and gates the UI: a loading spinner while auth state resolves, LoginScreen when unauthenticated, and the full tabbed Navigation when authenticated. AuthContext wraps Firebase Auth (email/password) with Firestore-backed user profiles and an admin-only "View as Client" impersonation feature. ThemeContext provides a comprehensive Apple-style light/dark color system with AsyncStorage-persisted theme preference. Navigation builds a 5-tab bottom navigator with per-tab native stacks and a custom iOS-style tab bar featuring a raised circular center "Home" button. The code is clean and consistent but has a few real defects (notably broken color references in the ViewModeBanner) and unpersisted impersonation/theme-context edge cases.

features.name: Email/Password Sign-In
features.description: User enters email + password on LoginScreen; signIn() calls Firebase signInWithEmailAndPassword, then loads the Firestore user profile. Errors are mapped to friendly messages (invalid-email, user-not-found, wrong-password, too-many-requests) and shown via Alert with haptic feedback. Success triggers a success haptic and onAuthStateChanged flips the app into the authenticated tree.

portability: High-value, reusable assets worth harvesting in a rewrite: (1) The full Apple-style design token system in ThemeContext.js / theme.js — light+dark palettes with system backgrounds, labels, fills, separators, semantic colors, grays, plus Carben brand orange, and a clean automatic/light/dark resolution with AsyncStorage persistence. This is the most laborious and polished artifact here. (2) The CustomTabBar with the raised circular center button, themed focus icons, haptics, and keyboard-aware hide logic — a non-trivial custom component. (3) The tab-blur stack-reset logic in navigation.js (targeting the child navigator key for StackActions.popToTop) is a subtle, hard-won React Navigation pattern worth keeping. (4) The 'View as Client' admin impersonation model in AuthContext (isAdmin vs isRealAdmin separation, originalAdmin stash/restore) is a clean pattern even if it needs persistence. (5) Firebase Auth + AsyncStorage persistence wiring (initializeAuth + getReactNativePersistence) and the friendly error-code mapping. (6) The navigationRef-to-NotificationContext deep-link wiring.
notes: Code quality overall is good: consistent style, clear comments, sensible context boundaries, haptics and Apple-style polish throughout. Key risks for a rewrite/maintainer: (1) The ViewModeBanner color bug (COLORS.carbenOrange / COLORS.white undefined) is a live defect that should be fixed first — the impersonation banner likely renders broken. (2) Impersonation and (potentially) auth recovery rely on in-memory state that does not survive reloads; treat as ephemeral. (3) Secrets are committed in config/firebase.js. (4) Heavy duplication in navigation.js — shared screens (Calendar, Profile, PrivacyPolicy, TermsOfService, Conversation, ProjectDetail) are registered in 4-5 stacks; a shared root stack or screen group would reduce drift. (5) Provider nesting order matters: Theme is outermost so App.js loading spinner can use colors before auth resolves; QuickBooks/Notification depend on Auth being above them. (6) Several Platform.OS Android branches exist despite the app being iOS-targeted. (7) The cached userProfile write with no read is a small landmine suggesting an intended-but-unfinished offline path.

area: Projects subsystem (Home hub, project list/filtering, project detail, project creation, photo management)
summary: The Projects subsystem is the core of the Carben Connect mobile app: a Firebase-backed (Firestore + Storage) construction project-management flow spanning a Home hub, a searchable/filterable project list, a project detail view, a creation form, and a standalone photo-upload screen. It is dual-role aware (admin vs client) via useAuth().isAdmin(), with admins seeing all projects and clients scoped to their own clientId. Projects live in the `projects` Firestore collection and integrate adjacent collections (users, locations, invoices, messages) and external accounting systems (QuickBooks, FreshBooks) whose IDs/PDF links are surfaced read-only in the UI. Real-time listeners (onSnapshot) power the list and home counts; detail/photo screens use one-shot getDocs/getDoc. The code is functional and reasonably polished visually (consistent theme tokens, haptics throughout) but carries notable gaps: a known-broken unread-message count, a stubbed messageCount, hardcoded phone numbers, a non-functional pull-to-refresh, and a client-side filtering/sorting model that will not scale.

portability: Worth harvesting in a rewrite: (1) The dual-role (admin/client) data-scoping pattern used consistently across all screens (admin = full collection query, client = where clientId == userProfile.id) — this access model is reusable. (2) The QuickBooks/FreshBooks integration surface: the project schema's reconciliation of multiple external systems (qbCustomerId/qbCustomerName, quickbooksInvoiceNumber, quickbooksEstimateNumber, freshbooksInvoiceNumber, invoicePdfLink/estimatePdfLink, invoices.matchedToProject) and the contractorIds=all-admins convention required for website cross-app compatibility represent hard-won integration knowledge. (3) The photo capture+upload pipeline (expo-image-picker -> fetch(uri) -> blob -> Firebase Storage uploadBytes -> getDownloadURL -> arrayUnion into Firestore) is a clean, reusable recipe; AddPhotosScreen's richer photo-object form (with uploadedBy metadata) is the better template. (4) The design-token system (TYPOGRAPHY/SPACING/RADIUS/SHADOWS/TAB_BAR_HEIGHT from ../theme, iOS semantic colors via ThemeContext with light/dark createStyles(colors) pattern) is mature and consistent across the whole subsystem. (5) The VoiceRecorder -> {title, description, transcription} contract feeding project creation is a differentiated feature worth preserving. (6) The expandable client>location filter dropdown in ProjectsScreen is non-trivial UI logic.
notes: Code quality is mid: visually polished and consistent (theme tokens, haptics on nearly every interaction, good empty/loading states), but architecturally naive in data handling. Key risks for a rewrite: (1) All search/filter/sort is in-memory client-side over the full project set — fine for tens of projects, will not scale to hundreds and defeats Firestore pagination. (2) Schema drift is pervasive — projects come from at least four sources (manual app creation, website import, QuickBooks, FreshBooks) and the UI defensively OR's overlapping fields (totalAmount/estimatedTotal/totalPrice, title/name, photo URL-string vs object, txnDate vs createdAt, clientName-on-doc vs clients-lookup). A rewrite should normalize this schema first. (3) The repeated 'avoiding Firestore permission issues' / hardcoded values / 'this is why projects don't show on website' comments signal that Firestore security rules and the website data contract are brittle and were patched reactively — audit rules and define a canonical project schema before porting. (4) Detail and AddPhotos screens use one-shot reads (getDoc/getDocs) while the list uses onSnapshot, so the detail view can show stale data after a list-side change. (5) Deletes are destructive with no cleanup of Storage/messages/invoices, creating orphans. (6) Two separate photo-add paths (NewProject and AddPhotos) with divergent data shapes should be unified. (7) Heavy reliance on stable-but-undeclared hook deps (isAdmin) and empty dep arrays referencing userProfile is a stale-closure footgun.

summary: The Estimates Engine is an admin-only, tabbed workspace for turning a project into a priced estimate and pushing it to QuickBooks. EstimateWorkspaceScreen wires four live tabs (Overview, Estimate, Calculator, QuickBooks) driven by a real-time estimateProgress document that tracks step completion and lights up checkmarks. The active flow is: review project/customer context, write or AI-generate an estimate description (auto-saved + finalize toggle), build a costed calculator (Materials, Subcontractors, Labor, Profit with markups and auto-save), then run a pre-flight checklist, assign a QuickBooks customer fetched from a backend REST API, and POST the estimate to QuickBooks. AI features (estimate generation and an in-context chat assistant) call a remote Carben Connect backend at carbenconnect.com rather than OpenAI directly. Three components in the folder (PricingCalculatorTab, EstimateDescriptionTab, ProjectInfoTab) are orphaned dead code superseded by the AIEstimateTab/CalculatorTab/ProjectOverviewTab that the screen actually imports.

Similarly there are two description editors (AIEstimateTab live, EstimateDescriptionTab dead) and two overview tabs (ProjectOverviewTab live, ProjectInfoTab dead) — the dead trio should be deleted. The subsystem is admin-only (isAdmin gate) and entirely client-driven: all AI and QuickBooks logic lives behind the carbenconnect.com backend (no API keys in the app, good), but that backend is the source of truth for OAuth, estimate creation, and the estimates/{projectId} write that this code only reads. summary: This subsystem provides in-app messaging between clients and admins, plus Expo push notifications. The Inbox lists conversations (grouped by project, or by client for general messages) using a real-time Firestore listener on the `messages` collection; tapping a card opens the ConversationScreen, a chat-bubble thread with a docked composer. NewMessageScreen lets a user start a thread optionally attached to a project. Push notifications are handled client-side by NotificationContext (token registration, permission prompt, tap routing) and server-side by Firebase Cloud Functions in functions/notificationFunctions.js that fire on new messages/estimates/projects and POST to Expo's push API. DraftsScreen is included in the file set but is actually an admin estimate-pipeline screen, not messaging; it is admin-gated and was de-linked from the UI per the latest commit. Notably there is NO read/unread persistence — "unread" is computed heuristically on the fly and never written back, so messages are never actually marked read.

Pull-to-refresh exists but is cosmetic since the onSnapshot listener already streams updates. Tapping a card navigates to Conversation. Header has New Message, Calendar, and Profile buttons.

features.name: Unread / read status
features.description: Unread is derived purely at read time in InboxScreen: a conversation is 'unread' if the latest admin message is newer than the latest client message (or no client reply yet). MessageCard reads message.unread for styling but the Inbox overrides it with its computed value; ConversationScreen writes read:false/unread:true on every send and NEVER updates them. Opening a conversation does not mark anything read. So unread state is heuristic, asymmetric (only works from the client's perspective; admin viewing all messages gets the same logic), and the persisted read/unread fields are effectively dead.

portability: The Expo push pipeline is the most reusable asset: client-side token registration + permission flow + Firestore token storage (contexts/NotificationContext.js), the server-side sender helper that batches/validates ExponentPushToken-prefixed tokens and POSTs to https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send (functions/sendPushNotification.js), and the Firestore onCreate triggers that fan out to recipients (functions/notificationFunctions.js). The notification-tap deep-link router (type -> tab+screen+params) and the navigationRef pattern wired from navigation.js are worth keeping. The ConversationScreen composer UX is well-built and harvestable: KeyboardAvoidingView + tab-bar-aware inputPadBottom math, interactive keyboard dismiss, auto-scroll-to-end, optimistic send with rollback, and date-separator grouping. DraftsScreen's 5-stage estimate progress model (20% per stage: descriptionGenerated/descriptionFinalized/calculatorStarted/calculatorComplete/sentToQuickBooks) and its status-label/color mapping encode real business logic worth preserving. The theme-token usage (TYPOGRAPHY/SPACING/RADIUS/SHADOWS, iOS-style semantic colors) is consistent and portable.
notes: Biggest architectural risk: there is no canonical 'conversations' collection — conversations are reconstructed at runtime by grouping a flat messages collection, with unread computed heuristically and never persisted. This means no reliable unread badges, no scalable pagination, and per-conversation queries that load full history. The client/admin asymmetry (clients filtered by clientId, admins read ALL messages with orderBy) requires a composite index and will not scale. createdAt uses client Date() instead of serverTimestamp, so ordering is clock-dependent. The general-message path (projectId null) is only partially supported: Inbox/Conversation handle it, but the message-push Cloud Function does not, and the cloud function's admin recipients depend on a contractorIds field the app never writes — so admin push for messages is likely silently broken. DraftsScreen is mis-bundled with messaging (it is the estimate pipeline) and appears orphaned after the recent nav cleanup. expoPushToken and EAS projectId are hardcoded/global. Several screens have incomplete useEffect dependency arrays creating stale-closure bugs. Overall the UI layer is polished and complete; the data model and notification reliability are where a rewrite should focus.

summary: The Clients subsystem lets admins browse a directory of client users, drill into an individual client to see their contact/QuickBooks info and associated projects, and (via a selector modal) impersonate/"view as" a specific client. A separate ClientSummary component renders an AI-generated, project-linked status paragraph on the client's own homepage. All client records live in the Firestore `users` collection filtered by `role == 'client'`; projects are read from the `projects` collection by `clientId`. The subsystem is read-only from the mobile side: there is no create/edit/delete client capability anywhere despite empty-state copy implying it. The AI summary is the only feature that calls an external service (a Cloud Function wrapping an LLM).

portability: The genuinely valuable, non-trivial pieces to harvest: (1) The QuickBooks data-shape handling that gracefully supports three formats (qbCustomers array with multiple/single locations, legacy qbCustomerId, legacy qbLocationName) — this dual-format migration logic is duplicated in ClientCard and ClientDetailScreen and represents real domain knowledge about the data's evolution. (2) The ClientSummary inline project-link parser: the regex /([^\[]+)\[([a-zA-Z0-9]+)\]/g that turns 'Project Title[projectId]' markers from an LLM response into tappable navigation links is a clean, reusable pattern for rendering AI text with embedded entity links, plus the cache-source indicator UX. (3) The generateClientSummary Cloud Function wiring (httpsCallable contract: send {userId}, receive {summary, source}). (4) The consistent iOS-style design-token usage (TYPOGRAPHY/SPACING/RADIUS/SHADOWS from ../theme) and avatar-from-initial pattern reused across cards/modal/detail.
notes: This subsystem is read-only and fairly polished visually but shallow functionally. Key risks for a rewrite: (1) Theming inconsistency — ClientSelectorModal alone uses the legacy static COLORS module while everything else uses dynamic useTheme(); this is a dark-mode bug. (2) Two different client-data access patterns coexist: the list passes the entire client object through navigation params (stale, no live updates on the detail card) while projects use live listeners — re-fetching the client by id would be more correct. (3) The non-admin query targets a stored 'id' field instead of doc id, a fragile data-modeling assumption. (4) Pull-to-refresh is decorative on both screens because onSnapshot already streams. (5) No client CRUD exists despite UI copy implying an add flow — confirm whether client creation is intentionally backend/web-only. (6) ProjectCard is always rendered with isAdmin={false}, so admin context is lost when viewing projects through a client. (7) Client privacy/security depends entirely on Firestore rules since the mobile non-admin path filters client-side with a where clause that could be bypassed if rules are lax. Overall: solid presentational layer, thin logic, a few correctness/theming bugs, and a notable missing write path.

summary: This subsystem provides admin-only accounting integrations for the Carben Connect app. There are two distinct integrations of very different maturity. The QuickBooks integration (QuickBooksScreen.js + QuickBooksContext.js) is essentially a settings/credentials UI shell: it persists configuration to Firestore but its core actions (Connect, Test Connection, Sync Now) are placeholders/simulations, while a separate context layer (QuickBooksContext) wires up real automatic OAuth token-refresh against a Cloud Function. The FreshBooks integration (FreshBooksScreen.js) is the genuinely functional one: it performs a real OAuth connect/disconnect via Cloud Functions, fetches invoices with date-range and pagination, lets admins map each invoice to a client (and a client location), bulk-imports invoices as projects/estimates, and offers a destructive "clear all imported data" action. All UI follows a shared iOS-style design system (TYPOGRAPHY/SPACING/RADIUS/SHADOWS theme tokens) and is gated behind isAdmin().

portability: The FreshBooks integration is the genuinely hard-won, harvest-worthy piece: a complete Cloud-Functions-backed OAuth flow (freshbooksConnect returning an authUrl opened via Linking, freshbooksCallback redirect handling, freshbooksDisconnect), invoice retrieval with date-range + pagination (freshbooksGetInvoices, perPage 50), and a full bulk-import pipeline (freshbooksBulkImport) that maps external invoices to internal clients/locations and creates projects+estimates, plus a destructive cleanup (freshbooksClearImported). The QuickBooksContext token-refresh pattern is also worth keeping: onSnapshot-driven connection detection, AppState 'active' foreground re-check, a 30-minute pre-expiry refresh window, in-flight guard (isRefreshing), and httpsCallable 'refreshQuickBooksToken' — a clean, generic OAuth-token-keep-alive harness adaptable to any provider. The shared iOS design tokens (TYPOGRAPHY/SPACING/RADIUS/SHADOWS, themed createStyles(colors)) and the settings-card/section/status-card/danger-zone UI patterns are consistent and reusable.
notes: The two integrations are at opposite maturity levels and should not be conflated: FreshBooks is feature-complete and backed by real Cloud Functions; QuickBooks is a UI shell whose three primary buttons (Connect, Test, Sync) are placeholders/simulations, even though a sophisticated QuickBooksContext token-refresh layer exists and is real. That asymmetry strongly implies QuickBooks was scaffolded UI-first and never finished server-side, while the context was built speculatively (and currently has nothing to refresh because no real tokens are ever produced by the screen). SECURITY RISK: QuickBooks clientSecret/accessToken/refreshToken are written to Firestore in plaintext from the client and re-read into TextInputs — anyone with read access to settings/quickbooks gets the secrets; this should move to server-side secret storage. The FreshBooks redirectUri and the Cloud Functions project/region are hardcoded ('carben-connect', 'us-central1'), which will break in other environments. The screen reads a settings/freshbooks doc directly but mutations go through Cloud Functions — good separation; QuickBooks instead mutates Firestore directly from the client, which is inconsistent and riskier. Cross-coupling: the FreshBooks import reuses a field named qbCustomers (QuickBooks customers) for client locations, indicating shared client schema where QB customers double as locations. Numerous handlers silently no-op when a Cloud Function returns success:false (no error surfaced). Two duplicate StyleSheet keys (invoiceHeader in FreshBooks, paddingBottom in QuickBooks) are latent bugs/dead code. The FreshBooks ScrollView uses style instead of contentContainerStyle for bottom padding, which likely doesn't render as intended. A rewrite should: finish or remove the QuickBooks server side, encrypt/relocate secrets, add real date pickers + working pagination to FreshBooks, externalize the hardcoded URLs, and unify the direct-Firestore vs Cloud-Function mutation patterns.

summary: The AI & Voice subsystem lets contractors create projects by speaking and lets them generate/refine construction estimate descriptions with AI. It is implemented as a thin React Native client that posts to Vercel-hosted HTTP endpoints at carbenconnect.com/api/ai/* (transcribe, generate-project, generate-estimate, chat) which proxy to OpenAI (Whisper for speech-to-text, GPT-4o for generation/chat). Voice recording uses expo-audio; the resulting m4a is uploaded as multipart form data, transcribed, then fed to a project-generation endpoint that returns a structured title/description/summary. A parallel, fully-built set of Firebase Callable Functions (transcribeAudio, generateProject, textToSpeech) exists in functions/index.js but is NOT called by the mobile app — the app exclusively uses the Vercel HTTP API. config/openai.js exposes generateProject/transcribeAudio/aiChat helpers that are dead code (only generateEstimate is imported anywhere). lib/api.ts is a generic fetch wrapper that is also unused by this subsystem.

This means the Firebase functions (including textToSpeech, which has no client at all) are dead weight or an abandoned migration; a rewrite must decide on one. The client hardcodes endpoint hosts inconsistently (carbenconnect.com vs www.carbenconnect.com) and never routes AI calls through the otherwise-well-built lib/api.ts, so there is no timeout, retry, or auth header on any AI/voice request (the Vercel endpoints appear to be unauthenticated, unlike the auth-gated Firebase functions — a security consideration since they call paid OpenAI APIs). config/openai.js is mostly dead code (3 of 4 exports unused) and its aiChat helper's body shape ('history') does not even match the live API ('conversationHistory'). Voice transcription is silently injected into the project 'messages' inbox as a SYSTEM message labeled 'Voice Transcription' — a non-obvious side effect a rewrite must preserve or intentionally drop. Chat history and additional-instructions are ephemeral (never persisted). Error messages leak server config details to end users. Overall the happy paths are functional and reasonably polished (haptics, loading states, auto-save), but the subsystem carries significant duplication and dead code, and the contract between client and the Vercel API is loosely defined (response keys are guessed via fallback chains).

summary: This subsystem covers the app's administrative tooling, user account UI, app preferences, and static legal/utility screens. The core admin feature is user management: an admin-only list of all Firestore `users` with search/filter/stats (UserManagementScreen) feeding into a per-user editor (UserEditScreen) that can update profile fields, trigger Firebase Auth password reset emails, force-change a password via a `changeUserPassword` Cloud Function, and delete user docs. MoreScreen is the navigation hub (profile, theme switching, admin links to User Management/QuickBooks/FreshBooks/Drafts, support links, sign out) and ProfileScreen offers profile viewing plus an admin "View as Client" impersonation flow backed by AuthContext. SettingsScreen, CalendarScreen, PrivacyPolicyScreen, and TermsOfServiceScreen are largely presentational: Settings has non-persisted toggles and placeholder actions, Calendar is a self-contained month grid with no real event data, and the two legal screens are hardcoded static text. There is a noticeable split between genuinely wired admin features and decorative/stub UI.

summary: The Firebase Cloud Functions backend (Node 20, firebase-functions v4) provides server-side capabilities the React Native client cannot do safely on-device: admin user management (password changes, welcome emails), AI features via OpenAI (Whisper transcription, GPT-4o project generation, TTS), accounting integrations (QuickBooks token refresh, full FreshBooks OAuth + invoice import pipeline), and Firestore-triggered Expo push notifications for messages, estimates, and new projects. Almost all callable functions gate on a Firebase Auth token plus an 'admin' role lookup in the Firestore users collection, and write an audit trail to audit_logs for sensitive actions. The most substantial and complete subsystem is the FreshBooks integration (connect, OAuth callback, token refresh, list invoices, single/bulk import as projects+estimates, disconnect, clear-imported). Notable risks: hardcoded FreshBooks client ID/secret committed in source, an OpenAI placeholder API key fallback, and a fragile internal use of `.run()` for bulk import.

OpenAI API key falls back to a placeholder 'sk-placeholder-for-local-analysis' if config/env not set, which will cause silent auth failures rather than a clear startup error.

Bulk import uses exports.freshbooksImportInvoice.run(importData, context) — non-standard internal invocation of a Gen1 onCall handler; fragile and likely broken. Shared import logic should be extracted into a plain async helper.
freshbooksCallback hardcodes redirectUri to the cloud function URL, ignoring the redirectUri persisted during freshbooksConnect; if the connect-time URI differs, token exchange may mismatch.
sendWelcomeEmail does not actually send an email — it only returns a reset link and notes the app must send it via an external service. No email provider wired.
onMessageCreated assumes message.projectId exists; general messages without projectId (supported per recent commits c97fee0/1921c3e) will hit a failed project lookup and silently skip notification.
freshbooksClearImported deletes via a single Firestore batch with no 500-op chunking; will throw if projects+estimates deletes exceed 500.

QuickBooks integration is only token-refresh; no connect/OAuth-callback/list/import functions exist (unlike FreshBooks), and refreshQuickBooksToken depends on settings/quickbooks fields (refreshToken, clientId, clientSecret) presumably populated elsewhere.
Push notification triggers swallow all errors and return null (no retry, no dead-letter, no surfacing). Acceptable for fire-and-forget but means failures are invisible beyond logs.
onProjectCreated fires for every project insert including FreshBooks bulk-imported projects, which can mass-notify all admins during an import.
Whisper transcription hardcodes language:'en'; non-English voice notes will be mis-transcribed/translated.
refreshQuickBooksToken builds the request body via string interpolation of refreshToken without URL-encoding; a token containing reserved chars could break the form body.
sendPushNotification (single) does not validate the 'ExponentPushToken' prefix like the batch variant does, so a stale/invalid stored token is posted directly to Expo.
All functions are Gen1 firebase-functions v4 with no region pinning, memory/timeout config, or App Check; FreshBooks import + AI calls may exceed default timeout/memory.

portability: The FreshBooks integration is the clearly laborious, high-value piece worth harvesting: full OAuth lifecycle (authorize URL build at index.js:654-657, code-for-token exchange in the onRequest callback at 743-757, token refresh at 888-916, and a reusable inline 'refresh-if-within-1hr-of-expiry' pattern at 994-1029), plus the invoice normalization/transformation mapping (1056-1076) and the invoice->project+estimate import mapping including line-item conversion (1199-1259). The styled HTML success/error OAuth callback pages (704-836) are reusable UX. The QuickBooks bearer-token refresh (Basic-auth + form-encoded grant_type=refresh_token, 515-551) is a clean reference for Intuit OAuth. The OpenAI wiring is also reusable: the base64-audio -> Readable-stream-with-fake-.path Whisper trick (235-255), the GPT-4o JSON-mode contractor prompt templates for both new and incremental project descriptions (305-374), and the TTS base64 round-trip (427-441). The Expo push helper (sendPushNotification.js) with token-prefix filtering and the admin-role-gating + audit_logs pattern (repeated across every admin callable) are clean, portable building blocks.
notes: Architecture is a single 1539-line index.js plus two notification modules; consistent and readable but monolithic. Every admin-sensitive callable repeats the identical auth-check + role lookup boilerplate — a candidate for a shared assertAdmin(context) helper. Error handling is consistently good in callables (re-throws HttpsError, wraps others, logs) but notification triggers intentionally swallow errors. Mixed HTTP clients: axios (FreshBooks), global fetch (QuickBooks, Node 20), and node-fetch (Expo helper) — three different fetch mechanisms in one codebase. Security risks a rewrite must address: (1) committed FreshBooks secrets at index.js:631-634 must move to Secret Manager / functions config and be rotated; (2) the OpenAI placeholder-key fallback should fail loudly instead; (3) no App Check on any callable. Correctness risks: freshbooksBulkImport's `.run()` call is the most likely runtime failure; the single-batch delete in clear-imported won't scale past 500 docs; and onMessageCreated won't notify for the app's newly-supported general (project-less) messages. The functions are Gen1 (firebase-functions ^4.5.0) — a rewrite should consider Gen2 with explicit region, memory, timeout, and secrets binding. Deploy/test tooling is standard (firebase emulators, functions:shell, deploy, log) and firebase-functions-test is installed though no test files were referenced here.

summary: This subsystem provides the foundational design tokens, shared UI components, Firebase/data-layer wiring, and security rules for the Carben Connect Mobile 2.0 app. theme.js defines an Apple-HIG-based token set (typography, semantic light/dark colors, spacing, radius, shadows, animation, touch targets). config/firebase.js initializes Firebase (Auth with AsyncStorage persistence, Firestore, Storage, Functions). firestore.rules / storage.rules / firestore.indexes.json define access control and query indexes. A handful of branded components (BrandWelcomeHeader, GlowingCallButton, StripedCallButton, VoiceRecorder) and utilities (lib/images.ts image compression, lib/secureStore.ts keychain wrapper, AppErrorBoundary) round out the layer. VoiceRecorder is the most substantial feature, wiring expo-audio recording to remote AI transcription + project-generation endpoints. Notable risks: the color tokens are duplicated (not shared) between theme.js and ThemeContext.js, the Firebase API key is hardcoded in source, and secureStore is fully implemented but unused.

portability: High-value to harvest: (1) The full Apple-HIG design token set in theme.js — typography scale with exact letterSpacing/lineHeight, light+dark iOS semantic color palettes, spacing/radius/shadow/animation/touch-target constants — is a complete, reusable design system. (2) VoiceRecorder.js is the most laborious piece: a working expo-audio record/permission/audio-mode lifecycle plus the two-step AI pipeline (multipart m4a upload to a transcription endpoint, then JSON call to a project-generation endpoint returning title/description/summary) — the React-Native FormData file-append pattern (uri/type/name) and the transcribe→generate flow are worth keeping verbatim. (3) lib/images.ts compression presets (1600px/75% upload, 400px/60% thumbnail with graceful fallback) are tuned and reusable. (4) lib/secureStore.ts is a clean, ready-to-use Keychain wrapper with web fallback. (5) GlowingCallButton's self-measuring onLayout height-proportional scaling (radius/padding/font/icon/halo) and the gradient-border + halo glow technique are non-trivial custom UI. (6) Firestore/Storage rules encode the real role model (admin via users.role, owner-locked project state fields approved/paid/finalized, per-bucket size/content-type limits) and are worth porting as the security baseline.
notes: Code quality is generally clean and well-commented, but the design layer has a significant structural smell: theme.js and ThemeContext.js maintain duplicate color palettes, and theme.js's COLORS/COLORS_DARK/getTheme are largely vestigial — dark mode actually flows through ThemeContext's useTheme hook. Any component importing the static COLORS export silently breaks dark mode. The Firebase config (including API key) is committed in plaintext; while Firebase web API keys are not strictly secret, security depends entirely on the rules files in this subsystem, so the broad 'any authed' read on projects and the unguarded update on top-level messages are the real exposure. VoiceRecorder depends on external Vercel endpoints at carbenconnect.com (no auth token sent, no retry/timeout), so it will silently fail if those endpoints change or the device is offline; its 'functions/unauthenticated' error branch is dead since it uses plain fetch, not Firebase callables. secureStore and createThumbnail are implemented-but-unused, suggesting planned-but-abandoned features. The component library is small and stylistically consistent (haptics, theme-awareness, gradient branding in orange #F97316 / blue #3B82F6). A rewrite should consolidate to a single theme source, externalize endpoint URLs/config, add Sentry per the existing TODO, and tighten the messages/projects Firestore rules.
